schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    PLAYER_ID INT,
    EVENT_DATE DATE,
    DEVICE_ID INT,
    GAMES_PLAYED INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE),
    CHECK (GAMES_PLAYED >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT A1.FIRST_LOGIN AS INSTALL_DT, COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID) AS INSTALLS, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN (A1.FIRST_LOGIN + 1) = A2.EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/ COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID)), 2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS FIRST_LOGIN FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) AS A1 JOIN ACTIVITY AS A2 ON A1.PLAYER_ID = A2.PLAYER_ID GROUP BY A1.FIRST_LOGIN
q2: WITH TEMP AS (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS INSTALL_DATE FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) SELECT INSTALL_DATE AS INSTALL_DT, SUM(CASE WHEN INSTALL_DATE=EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS INSTALLS, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN INSTALL_DATE+1=EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END )/SUM(CASE WHEN INSTALL_DATE=EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM TEMP JOIN ACTIVITY A ON TEMP.PLAYER_ID=A.PLAYER_ID GROUP BY INSTALL_DATE

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 counts distinct players per install date for INSTALLS, while Q2 counts event occurrences on install dates. DAY1_RETENTION denominators differ: Q1 uses COUNT(DISTINCT PLAYER_ID), Q2 uses SUM(CASE WHEN INSTALL_DATE=EVENT_DATE THEN 1 END). This leads to different retention rates when players have multiple events on their install date.
